title: RuleCandidate
description: A PROPOSED deterministic rule generated from a PatternCandidate — proposed, NOT active (status defaults to 'proposed'; an LLM may PROPOSE the rule body via the single LLMGateway, but proposing is not promoting). It carries the rule body (decision_table / authority / threshold / routing / ...), its scope, worked examples AND counterexamples, the expected failure modes, a REQUIRED fallback_policy (every active rule must have a deterministic-first-then-fallback path), and — critically — distilled_from_trace_ids + distilled_from_pattern_id, the LOSSLESS link back to the LLM/consensus/adjudication traces it was distilled from (a promoted rule NEVER deletes them). A truth-serving rule (rule_class=truth_serving) demands the strictest promotion bar (near-zero FP + first-promotion human review). tenant_private source_scope cannot yield a global rule unless anonymized + approved. Deterministic when created_at is injected.

rule_candidate_id.description: content-addressed id over (rule_body + scope + distilled_from_pattern_id); deterministic

source_scope.description: tenant_private can NOT yield a global rule unless anonymized + approved (replay/promotion enforce)

rule_type.description: the deterministic mechanism this rule uses

rule_class.description: the risk class that sets the promotion bar; truth_serving demands near-zero FP + human review for first promotion

scope.description: where the rule applies (e.g. 'conflict_type=deadline_mismatch on global_public CFPB facts'); narrow scope = safer rule

input_fields.description: the input fields the rule reads

output_decision.description: the deterministic decision the rule produces (e.g. 'winner=higher_authority_source, loser=held_out')

rule_body.description: the executable/serializable rule definition (a handle or canonical text); the deterministic mechanism, not an LLM prompt

examples.description: worked positive examples the rule must reproduce

from_trace_id.description: the verified trace this example came from (lossless link)

counterexamples.description: cases the rule must ABSTAIN on or decide differently (e.g. ambiguous authority, novel doc type); present even if empty

must_not_decide.description: the WRONG decision the rule must never produce here

expected_behavior.description: what the rule should do instead

expected_failure_modes.description: the ways this rule could be wrong (ambiguous authority, stale fact, OOD inputs); informs replay/shadow scrutiny; present even if empty

fallback_policy.description: REQUIRED: the deterministic-first-then-fallback path; every active rule must have one (no active rule without a fallback)

policy_id.description: link to the FallbackPolicy this references, when one is registered

status.description: lifecycle; NOT 'active'/'promoted' by default — a candidate is born 'proposed'

proposed_by.description: who proposed the body; an LLM may propose, but proposing is not promoting

distilled_from_pattern_id.description: the PatternCandidate this rule was distilled from (lossless link)

distilled_from_trace_ids.description: the LLM/consensus/adjudication WorkflowTrace ids this rule was distilled from; NEVER deleted on promotion (lossless)
